content:
maya: Heads up — we saw a spike of schema::validation_error on tool-invoke for a subset of traffic in eu-west this morning. Fallbacks kicked in and routed ~12% of requests to degen models. Billing blip noticed.
liam: saw the alert. any pattern? model, route, customer tier?
maya: primarily hosted-api route /v1/chat with fncall enabled. Most are small seq_len but variety of tool shapes.
olga: graph from the console shows a cluster around 04:10 UTC. I can add a stacked series for strict vs soft validate counts.
rory: do we have the exact telemetry key? currently we emit `validation_reason` = "schema_mismatch" but it lacks granularity for arrays vs missing-prop vs type-mismatch.
liam: +1 on more granularity. also we should tag samples with `route_id` and `model_variant`.
paul: also include `fallback_reason` when fallback happened, otherwise it's hard to attribute cost.
maya: proposal: emit `validation_category` with values ["missing_field","type_mismatch","unexpected_array","extra_root"], keep `validation_mode` ["strict","soft"], and sample full payloads at 0.1% into secure bucket for debugging.
olga: console-wise I can: 1) make a new dashboard panel for validation_category breakdown; 2) add a heatmap for rate by route_id; 3) add a cost overlay for fallback volume. need the exact metric names.
rory: suggest metric namespace `invoke.validation.v1` and event fields: `category`, `mode`, `route_id`, `model`, `customer_tier`, `kvcache_hit`. we already have invoke.latency so stays consistent.
liam: what's the plan for alerting? current alert is a generic >5% rejects in 10m. that caused noisy pages.
paul: noisy pages because soft-rejects were counted same as hard. we should change alert to only count `mode=="strict"` or `category in [missing_field, unexpected_array]` as page-worthy. lower-level metrics can be an SLO burn signal.
maya: rollout plan: 1) wire new fields into telemetry (rory) 2) console panels (olga) 3) change alerting rule (paul + sres) 4) quick docs + FAQ for support + SEs 5) soft-validate default for hosted canary for 7 days, then evaluate.
liam: what's the sampling rate for payloads? 0.1% might still be big for high-volume customers. can we do dynamic sampling keyed by route_id where heavy routes sample less?
rory: yes, use reservoir sampling per route with caps. default 0.05% but for routes <1k reqs/day bump to 1%. implement in the telemetry client.
olga: UX ask: show a toggle in the console to switch between soft/strict view for historical charts so support can filter by mode. also allow quickly pivoting to affected customer list (not payloads) for privacy.
maya: privacy note — sampled payloads go to internal secure project with access controls and redaction pipeline. add a compliance tag to telemetry events `sensitivity: pii_filtered`.
paul: ops step: temporary mitigation — set routing fallback threshold higher for eu-west so we don't auto-degen at small blips. but keep canary for strict enforcement.
liam: are we comfortable changing routing thresholds? might hide real regressions. maybe only increase on a per-customer basis if SLA tier low.
maya: agreement: increase global degen threshold from 10% -> 20% for 30m in eu-west while we deploy telemetry, but do NOT change canary for premium customers. document the window and roll back automatically.
rory: I'll open a PR to telemetry schema and add tests. snippet: ```json
{"metric":"invoke.validation.v1","category":"missing_field","mode":"soft","route_id":"chat:default","model":"redwood-v1","count":1}
```
olga: I'll create dashboard draft and post link here when ready.
liam: we should also add a console annotation for the time window (04:00-04:30 UTC) so people see the spike context.
paul: setting pager to only trigger for strict/high-severity, updated runbook note to check validation_category and fallback_reason first.
maya: final action items: rory telemetry PR + unit tests; olga dashboard + annotation; paul update alerting and runbook; liam coordinate rollout throttle; maya publish support note and send SLA exceptions list. I'll update thread when PRs land. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy started: telemetry/agent v3.14 -> 04:45 UTC
rory: PR opened https://git.internal/r/telemetry/+/2345 (includes schema tests).
olga: dashboard draft https://console.internal/d/534/validation-errors now with category panel. feedback welcome.
liam: thanks all — good iterative approach, keep rollback ready.
maya: marking this resolved for now. will reopen if stats don't stabilize.
